summary: Bush bread, or seedcakes, refers to the bread made by Aboriginal Australians by crushing seeds into a dough that is then baked.
Bush tomatoes are the fruit or entire plants of certain nightshade (Solanum) species native to the more arid parts of Australia.
The witchetty grub (also spelled witchety grub or witjuti grub) is a term used in Australia for the large, white, wood-eating larvae of several moths.
Fina'denne' (many alternate spellings, commonly finadene, fina'denni', or fina'dene) is a spicy, all-purpose condiment that is a staple of Chamorro cuisine.
Guyuria are traditional Chamorro cookies.
Kelaguen is a Chamorro dish from the Mariana Islands eaten as a side dish or as a main course.

Bannock, skaan (or scone), Indian bread, alatiq, or frybread is a flatbread produced by the Indigenous peoples of the Americas now found throughout North America, including Inuit in Canada and Alaska,
Muktuk (anglicized from various names below) is a traditional food of Inuit and other circumpolar peoples, consisting of whale skin and blubber.
Boil up is a traditional Māori food from New Zealand.
Kānga pirau (which translates literally from Māori as rotten corn), is a fermented maize (corn) porridge dish which is considered a delicacy by many Māori people of New Zealand.
Kānga waru (waru means 'to scrape') is a type of pudding from New Zealand.
Pāua is the Māori name given to four New Zealand species of large edible sea snails, marine gastropod molluscs which belong to the family Haliotidae (in which there is only one genus, Haliotis).
Rēwena bread or Māori bread (Māori: parāoa rēwena; literally 'flour leaven') is a type of sourdough bread from New Zealand.
Bammy is a traditional Jamaican cassava flatbread descended from the simple flatbread called casabe, eaten by the Taínos, Jamaica's Indigenous people.

Casabe or cassava bread is a flatbread made of cassava, eaten across the Caribbean Basin and the Amazon.
Cauim is a traditional alcoholic beverage or beer of the Indigenous peoples in Brazil since pre-Columbian times.
Colada morada is a drink that is part of Ecuador's gastronomic culture along with t'anta wawa bread dolls.
Frybread (also spelled fry bread) is a dish of the indigenous people of North America that is a flat dough bread, fried or deep-fried in oil, shortening, or lard.
Jerk is a style of cooking native to Jamaica, in which meat is dry-rubbed or wet-marinated with a hot spice mixture called Jamaican jerk spice.
Maize (US: ; Zea mays), also known as corn, is a tall stout grass that produces cereal grain.
Maniçoba is a dish in Brazilian cuisine that is from the Brazilian state of Pará located in the Brazilian Amazon.
Maple syrup is a sweet syrup made from the sap of maple trees.
Mbeju is a starch cake sometimes made with fariña or manioc flour typical of Paraguay.
Moqueca (IPA: [moˈkɛkɐ] or IPA: [muˈkɛkɐ] depending on the dialect, also spelled muqueca) is a Brazilian seafood stew.
Paçoca, or meat paçoca or savory paçoca, is a typical Brazilian dish.
Pemmican () (also pemican in older sources) is a mixture of tallow, dried meat, and sometimes dried berries.
Haupia is the Hawaiian name for a traditional coconut pudding found throughout Polynesia.
ʻInamona is a condiment or relish used in traditional Hawaiian cooking made from seed kernels of the kukui nut (candlenuts) and sea salt.
Kūlolo is a Hawaiian dish made with taro and coconut.
